name: atomisp_cp_general_isp_parameters
prose: Slice cut the head: the real function is atomisp_cp_general_isp_parameters(asd, arg, css_param, from_user); the name atomisp_copy_isp_config does not exist in the tree. Precondition: when non-NULL, asd and css_param are valid (asd->run_mode and asd->isp are dereferenced); each non-NULL config pointer in arg points to a readable object of the matching size, in user memory when from_user is true and in kernel memory otherwise. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL immediately if arg, asd or css_param is NULL. Otherwise it goes through the config and table fields of arg in a fixed order (wb, ob, dp, dz, nr, ee, tnr, a3a, ctc, cnr, ecd, ynr, fc, macc, aa, anr, xnr, yuv2rgb_cc, rgb2yuv_cc, macc_table, xnr_table, r/g/b gamma tables, anr_thres); for each field that is non-NULL and for which from_user is true or the corresponding css_param->update_flag field is still NULL it copies the object into css_param with copy_from_compatible (copy_from_user when from_user, memcpy otherwise) and points the matching update_flag field at the copy in css_param. The dz_config field is only considered when asd->run_mode->val is not ATOMISP_RUN_MODE_VIDEO, and after copying it atomisp_check_zoom_region must accept it, otherwise a "crop region error!" message is logged and -EINVAL is returned (the dz bytes are already copied, its update_flag is not set). A failed copy returns -EFAULT at once: fields processed earlier stay applied, the failing and later ones are not. When every step passes and from_user is true, css_param->isp_config_id is set from arg->isp_config_id; the function then returns 0. No locks are taken and no memory is allocated or freed.

name: atomisp_css_cp_dvs2_coefs
prose: Real name atomisp_css_cp_dvs2_coefs(asd, coefs, css_param, from_user) (the name atomisp_cp_dvs2_coefs does not exist; slice cut the head). Precondition: asd and css_param are valid; coefs may be NULL; when from_user is true, coefs (on ISP2401 the structure copied from it) and the eight coefficient buffers (hor_coefs and ver_coefs odd/even real/imag) must be readable user memory of asd->params.dvs_hor_coef_bytes / dvs_ver_coef_bytes bytes, otherwise readable kernel memory. Postcondition: the current grid is cur = atomisp_css_get_dvs_grid_info(&asd->params.curr_grid_info). It returns 0 and changes nothing when coefs or cur is NULL, or when from_user is false and css_param->update_flag.dvs2_coefs is already set. Without IS_ISP2401 the grid in coefs is compared with cur; with IS_ISP2401 coefs is first copied into a local structure (-EFAULT with nothing changed if that copy fails) and the local grid is compared. A differing grid (size or memcmp) logs "dvs grid mismatch" and returns -EAGAIN with nothing changed; any of the eight coefficient pointers NULL returns -EINVAL with nothing changed. If css_param->dvs2_coeff is NULL it is allocated with ia_css_dvs2_coefficients_allocate (NULL result returns -ENOMEM with nothing changed). The eight coefficient blocks are then copied with copy_from_compatible; if any copy fails, css_param->dvs2_coeff (new or pre-existing) is freed and set to NULL and -EFAULT is returned. On success update_flag.dvs2_coefs is set to css_param->dvs2_coeff and 0 is returned. No locks are taken.

prose: Slice cut the head: the code in the slice is the function __destroy_pipes(asd); the name __destroy_streams_pipes_loop does not exist. Precondition: asd and asd->isp are valid. Postcondition: it loops over the ATOMISP_INPUT_STREAM_NUM entries asd->stream_env[i]. An entry whose stream pointer is non-NULL is skipped after logging "cannot destroy css pipes for stream[%d]". For every other entry it calls __destroy_stream_pipes, which for each non-NULL pipe calls ia_css_pipe_destroy (a nonzero result is logged and makes the helper return -EINVAL) and in every case sets that pipe pointer to NULL and update_pipe[i] to false. If the helper returns nonzero the function returns that value (-EINVAL) immediately and the later stream_env entries are not processed; otherwise it returns 0 (also when some entries were skipped). No locks are taken; no memory is freed here beyond what ia_css_pipe_destroy does.

name: isp_vmem_2d_store
prose: Slice cut the head: the code is the function isp_vmem_2d_store(ID, to, from, height, width, stride_to, stride_from) (the name vmem_store_block does not exist). Precondition: ID is less than N_ISP_ID, to is a VMEM address aligned to ISP_VEC_ALIGN, width and stride_to are multiples of ISP_NWAY (these four conditions are assert()s, which may be compiled out), and from points to at least stride_from*(height-1)+width readable t_vmem_elem elements. Postcondition: returns nothing. For each row h from 0 to height-1 and for each column c from 0 up to but excluding width in steps of ISP_NWAY it calls store_vector(ID, vp, &from[stride_from*h + c]), where vp starts at the row's destination and advances by ISP_VEC_ALIGN bytes per vector; the row destination itself advances by (stride_to / ISP_NWAY) * ISP_VEC_ALIGN bytes per row. store_vector packs ISP_NWAY elements and writes them to the ISP vector memory through the device store path (ia_css_device_store or hrt_master_port_store) with a udelay(1). Nothing is done when height or width is 0. No locks are taken and no references are taken or released.

name: calculate_stride
prose: Precondition: bits_per_pixel is at least 1 and, after the optional rounding below, at most HIVE_ISP_DDR_WORD_BITS (256), otherwise the division 256 / bits_per_pixel yields 0 and DIV_ROUND_UP divides by zero; pixels_per_line and align_in_bytes are positive and small enough that no signed 32-bit intermediate overflows. Postcondition: the function has no error path, takes no locks and touches no state. It computes pixels_per_line_padded = CEIL_MUL(pixels_per_line, align_in_bytes), which is the division-based rounding up to a multiple of align_in_bytes (not a bit mask, so align_in_bytes need not be a power of two; align_in_bytes == 0 gives 0). When raw_packed is false, bits_per_pixel is first rounded up to a multiple of 8. It then takes pixels_per_word = 256 / bits_per_pixel (integer division), words_per_line = DIV_ROUND_UP(pixels_per_line_padded, pixels_per_word), and returns HIVE_ISP_DDR_WORD_BYTES (256 / 8 = 32) * words_per_line.
contract: /*@ requires bits_per_pixel >= 1 && bits_per_pixel <= 256 && pixels_per_line >= 0 && pixels_per_line <= 1000000 && align_in_bytes >= 1 && align_in_bytes <= 1000; ensures result == 32 * (((((pixels_per_line + align_in_bytes - 1) / align_in_bytes) * align_in_bytes) + (256 / (raw_packed ? bits_per_pixel : ((bits_per_pixel + 7) / 8) * 8)) - 1) / (256 / (raw_packed ? bits_per_pixel : ((bits_per_pixel + 7) / 8) * 8))); */
note: reviewer MIXED: old prose used 128 (wrong; HIVE_ISP_DDR_WORD_BITS=256 at hive_isp_css_defs.h:21, BYTES=32; reviewer's 16 is also wrong) and 1024 bits (wrong); zero-divisor concern right; 'CEIL_MUL is bitwise' wrong: math_support.h:13-14 is division based

name: av7110_attach
prose: Precondition: dev is a probed saa7146 device and pci_ext->ext_priv holds the card name string; the module parameters budgetpatch, full_ts, adapter_nr, volume and tv_standard are readable. Postcondition: if budgetpatch is 1 on entry it is set to 0 and a hardware autodetection (resets the saa7146, programs and runs an RPS1 program with mdelay(10) twice) sets it back to 1 only when the GPIO3 test detects the budget patch. Then av7110 = kzalloc(); if that fails the function returns -ENOMEM at once, nothing has been acquired and dev->ext_priv is untouched. Otherwise dev->ext_priv is set to av7110 and the function acquires, in order: firmware (get_firmware), the DVB adapter, the i2c adapter, optionally the page table of the DMA3 buffer (full_ts or budgetpatch; failure leaves ret = -ENOMEM), a 8192-byte coherent DEBI buffer (dma_alloc_coherent), iobuf (vmalloc), then av7110_av_init, av7110_ca_init, av7110_bootarm, av7110_firmversion, the arm_mon kthread, av7110_register, av7110_init_v4l and frontend_init. On success it initialises the ioctl mutex, optionally av7110_ir_init, logs "found av7110-%d", increments av7110_num and returns 0. If any step after the kzalloc fails it returns a negative errno (-ENOMEM for the DEBI buffer, iobuf and page-table allocation failures, otherwise the failing call's error), after undoing, in reverse order, only the steps that had succeeded (for example arm thread sync, dvb_unregister, ca/av exit, vfree, dma_free_coherent, page table destroy when grabbing is set, i2c_del_adapter, dvb_unregister_adapter, put_firmware) and then kfree(av7110); dev->ext_priv is left pointing at the freed memory in that case.
note: reviewer RIGHT: kzalloc failure returns -ENOMEM before ext_priv is set and before anything is acquired (av7110.c:2427-2431); old prose lumped it with the unwinding; also budgetpatch is first cleared (2343) not only set

name: isc_try_fmt
prose: Precondition: isc and f are valid, isc->num_user_formats is at least 1, isc->current_subdev->sd is usable, and code is NULL or points to writable u32 storage. Postcondition: if f->type is not V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE it returns -EINVAL at once without touching isc->try_config or f. Otherwise it picks sd_fmt = the first user format with a RAW mbus code (may be NULL) and direct_fmt = find_format_by_fourcc(pixelformat) (may be NULL); if both exist and the module parameter sensor_preferred is set, sd_fmt becomes direct_fmt; if only direct_fmt exists, sd_fmt becomes direct_fmt. rlp_dma_direct_dump is set to true whenever sd_fmt == direct_fmt at that point, which includes the case where both are NULL; in that case sd_fmt is then set to the last user format (so direct dump is on for that fallback). It records sd_fmt in isc->try_config.sd_format, clamps f->fmt.pix width and height to isc->max_width / max_height, sets try_config.fourcc to the requested pixelformat, and if isc_try_validate_formats fails it replaces both pixelformat and try_config.fourcc with sd_fmt->fourcc and validates again. It then runs isc_try_configure_rlp_dma and isc_try_configure_pipeline, isc_try_fse, and calls the subdev pad op set_fmt in TRY mode. On success it refills f->fmt.pix from the returned mbus format, re-clamps width/height, sets field to V4L2_FIELD_NONE, computes bytesperline = (width * bpp_v4l2) >> 3 and sizeimage = ((width * bpp) >> 3) * height, stores the mbus code in *code when code is non-NULL and returns 0. On failure after the type check it returns the negative errno of the failing step (the second isc_try_validate_formats, the RLP/DMA or pipeline configuration, the subdev set_fmt, or -EINVAL if no format could be chosen) and zeroes isc->try_config; the "Could not find any possible format" error is logged for every failure except a set_fmt error (which is silent); f->fmt.pix may already have been modified (clamped size, replaced pixelformat).
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): direct dump is set at 897-898 when sd_fmt == direct_fmt, which is true for NULL == NULL, before the fallback at 904-909, so the fallback does have rlp_dma_direct_dump = true; earlier claims about early return / no log on set_fmt failure were already correct in the prose

name: imgu_css_cfg_acc
prose: Slice cut the head: the real function is imgu_css_cfg_acc(css, pipe, use, acc, acc_old, acc_user) (ipu3-css-params.c:1947-2697); the name imgu_css_acc_param does not exist. Whole function read. Precondition: css, pipe, acc are valid; use, acc_old and acc_user may be NULL (acc_user is dereferenced only when use is non-NULL and the corresponding use flag is set). Postcondition: it fills the accelerator parameter block *acc and returns 0, or returns -EINVAL part-way with *acc already partly modified. Steps: imgu_css_cfg_acc_stripe (nonzero gives -EINVAL); input feeder row stride and start address/pixel for both stripes from the input format and effective rectangle; then for each section (bnr, green_disparity, dm, ccm, gamma, csc, cds, shd, iefd, yds_c0, chnr_c0, y_ee_nr, yds, chnr, yds2, tcc, anr, awb_fr, ae, af, awb) it takes the values from acc_user when use && its use flag is set, else from acc_old when acc_old is non-NULL, else defaults (some sections then have frame widths, grid ends and per-stripe splits recomputed); the ytm table is filled with i*32 and disabled; dpc is zeroed unless use->acc_dpc is set, which returns -EINVAL. It returns -EINVAL when: stripe config fails; the shd grid width is <= 0 or its grid_height_per_slice is <= 0 or imgu_css_shd_ops_calc fails; use->acc_dpc is set; the BDS scale factor (effective height * granularity / bds height) is below IMGU_BDS_MIN_SF_INV or past the end of imgu_css_bds_configs; the awb_fr, af or awb grid width is <= 0; acc->stripe.bds_out_stripes[0].width <= 10; or imgu_css_awb_fr_ops_calc, imgu_css_af_ops_calc or imgu_css_awb_ops_calc fails. The anr block is enabled (search, transform, tile2strm enable = 1). No locks are taken, no memory is allocated.
note: slice cut head; real function imgu_css_cfg_acc; old prose described only the bds/anr/awb_fr/ae/af fragment and missed the other returns

name: ipu7_isys_csi2_get_remote_desc
prose: Slice cut the head: the real function is ipu7_isys_csi2_get_remote_desc(source_stream, csi2, source_entity, entry, nr_queues) (the name ipu7_get_stream_frame_desc_entry does not exist). Precondition: csi2, source_entity, entry and nr_queues are valid pointers; *entry is writable for one frame descriptor entry and *nr_queues holds the caller's current count. Postcondition: it returns -EPIPE if media_entity_to_v4l2_subdev(source_entity) is NULL or if the CSI-2 sink pad has no remote pad. Otherwise it calls the remote subdev's pad get_frame_desc op and returns its error code if nonzero. It returns -EINVAL (with an error log) if the descriptor type is not V4L2_MBUS_FRAME_DESC_TYPE_CSI2, if no entry has stream equal to source_stream (the first matching entry is used), or if the matched entry's bus.csi2.vc is >= IPU7_NR_OF_CSI2_VC. Otherwise it copies the matched entry into *entry, increments *nr_queues once for every descriptor entry (including the matched one) whose vc equals the matched entry's vc, and returns 0. *entry and *nr_queues are modified only in that final success step; no locks are taken.
note: slice cut head; real name ipu7_isys_csi2_get_remote_desc; old prose omitted the two -EPIPE returns (lines 500-506)

name: cedrus_hw_probe
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is cedrus_hw_probe(dev) (cedrus_hw.c:246-347). Precondition: dev points to a cedrus_dev whose dev and pdev are valid. Postcondition, by path: (1) no OF match data: returns -EINVAL, nothing acquired. (2) dev->capabilities is set from the variant; platform_get_irq(pdev, 0) returning a value <= 0 makes the function return that value, which is 0 (reported as success with nothing further initialised) or a negative errno. (3) devm_request_irq failure: returns its error. (4) of_reserved_mem_device_init failure other than -ENODEV: returns it (no release needed). (5) sunxi_sram_claim failure: releases only the reserved memory (of_reserved_mem_device_release) and returns the error. (6) devm_clk_get for ahb, mod, ram, devm_reset_control_get, devm_platform_ioremap_resource (PTR_ERR of the failure) or clk_set_rate on the mod clock failing: releases the SRAM (sunxi_sram_release) and the reserved memory and returns the error. (7) pm_runtime_enable is called; if pm_runtime_enabled() is then false, cedrus_hw_resume(dev->dev) is called and if it fails the function calls pm_runtime_disable, releases SRAM and reserved memory and returns the error. (8) Otherwise it returns 0. The IRQ and devm clocks, reset control and register mapping are devm-managed; the SRAM claim, reserved memory and runtime PM are released by cedrus_hw_remove. Clocks are enabled only if cedrus_hw_resume was called here.
note: reviewer RIGHT: early failures (variant/irq/request_irq/reserved-mem) release nothing and the old prose said everything is released; also irq_dec==0 returns 0; pm_runtime_disable is called only in the resume-failure path, which is reached exactly when PM was NOT enabled

name: tegra_channel_s_input

name: traffic_status_watchdog
prose: Precondition: padapter is valid, its mlmepriv.LinkDetectInfo holds the packet counters and the previous period's bBusyTraffic, and from_timer is 0 or nonzero. Postcondition: it first calls collect_traffic_statistics(padapter). If the adapter is in the _FW_LINKED state: busy threshold is 25 (10 if the previous LinkDetectInfo.bBusyTraffic is set); bBusyTraffic (and bRxBusyTraffic or bTxBusyTraffic) is set if NumRxOkInPeriod or NumTxOkInPeriod exceeds the threshold; the "higher" flags are set with a threshold of 4000. If NumRxUnicastOkInPeriod + NumTxOkInPeriod > 8 or NumRxUnicastOkInPeriod > 2 then bEnterPS = false and, only if bBusyTraffic was set, TrafficTransitionCount is raised to at least 4, incremented and capped at 30; otherwise TrafficTransitionCount is decremented by 2 (set to 0 if below 2) and bEnterPS becomes true exactly when it reaches 0, that is when it was 0, 1 or 2 before. When bEnterPS is true and from_timer is 0 it calls LPS_Enter(padapter, "TRAFFIC_IDLE"); when bEnterPS is true and from_timer is nonzero it makes no LPS call. When bEnterPS is false it calls LPS_Leave(padapter, "TRAFFIC_BUSY") if from_timer is 0, else rtw_lps_ctrl_wk_cmd(padapter, LPS_CTRL_TRAFFIC_BUSY, 1). If the adapter is not linked, the function tests only the _WIFI_ASOC_STATE bit of dvobj->padapters->mlmepriv (the first adapter of the device object, not every interface); LPS_Leave(padapter, "NON_LINKED") is called when from_timer is 0 and that bit is clear. bEnterPS stays false. Once it reaches the end of the function it zeroes NumRxOkInPeriod, NumTxOkInPeriod and NumRxUnicastOkInPeriod and stores this period's bBusyTraffic, bTxBusyTraffic, bRxBusyTraffic, bHigherBusyTraffic, bHigherBusyRxTraffic and bHigherBusyTxTraffic, and returns bEnterPS (1 only in the linked-and-idle case above, otherwise 0).
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the not-linked branch checks only dvobj->padapters (rtw_cmd.c:1203-1210); old prose said 'no interface is associated'

name: rtw_do_join
prose: Precondition: padapter is valid; the source comment says the caller already holds pmlmepriv->lock; the function itself takes and releases pmlmepriv->scanned_queue.lock (spin_lock_bh), so the caller must not hold that lock. Postcondition: at entry (under the scanned-queue lock) cur_network.join_res = -2, _FW_UNDER_LINKING is set in fw_state, pscanned = first list entry and to_join = true. The queue lock is released on each return before the function returns. (a) Scanned queue empty: the lock is dropped, _FW_UNDER_LINKING is cleared; if LinkDetectInfo.bBusyTraffic is false or rtw_to_roam(padapter) > 0 it returns the result of rtw_sitesurvey_cmd(assoc_ssid, 1, NULL, 0) and clears to_join if that result is not _SUCCESS (to_join stays true after a successful survey); otherwise to_join is cleared and it returns _FAIL. (b) Queue not empty: the lock is dropped and rtw_select_and_join_from_scanned_queue is called. On _SUCCESS to_join is cleared, the assoc timer is armed with MAX_JOIN_TIMEOUT, _FW_UNDER_LINKING stays set and _SUCCESS is returned. Otherwise, if fw_state has WIFI_ADHOC_STATE, fw_state is overwritten with WIFI_ADHOC_MASTER_STATE (which drops _FW_UNDER_LINKING), the registry dev_network is updated from assoc_ssid with a random IBSS address, and rtw_createbss_cmd is called: if it fails the function returns false (0, equal to _FAIL) with to_join still true; if it succeeds to_join is cleared and _SUCCESS is returned. If not ad-hoc, _FW_UNDER_LINKING is cleared and the same busy-traffic/roam test as in (a) decides between returning rtw_sitesurvey_cmd's result (to_join cleared only if it failed) and returning _FAIL with to_join cleared.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): _FW_UNDER_LINKING is cleared (lines 59, 112) before the site survey, so it does not remain set after a successful survey; _FAIL is 0 (osdep_service.h:11) so R1's 'ret=false not _FAIL' is moot

name: EXhalbtc8723b1ant_ScanNotify
prose: Precondition: pBtCoexist is valid with usable fBtcGet / fBtcRead1Byte / fBtcRead4Byte callbacks; type is any u8 (BTC_SCAN_START, BTC_SCAN_FINISH or other). Postcondition: returns nothing. If pBtCoexist->bManualControl or bStopCoexDm is set it returns at once. Otherwise: for type == BTC_SCAN_START it sets pCoexSta->bWiFiIsHighPriTask = true, calls halbtc8723b1ant_PsTdma(FORCE_EXEC, turn on = false, type 8) and reads registers 0x948 (4 bytes), 0x765 and 0x67 (1 byte), discarding the values; for any other type it sets bWiFiIsHighPriTask = false and stores BTC_GET_U1_AP_NUM into pCoexSta->nScanAPNum. Then, if btInfo.bBtDisabled is set it returns. Otherwise it reads the BT-HS-operation and wifi-connected flags, calls halbtc8723b1ant_QueryBtInfo and reads the wifi link status; if the link count (status >> 16) is at least 2 it calls LimitedTx(NORMAL_EXEC, 0, 0, 0, 0), LimitedRx(NORMAL_EXEC, false, false, 5) and ActionWifiMultiPort and returns; else if bC2hBtInquiryPage is set it calls ActionBtInquiry and returns; else if BT HS is on it calls ActionHs and returns; else for BTC_SCAN_START it calls ActionWifiNotConnectedScan or ActionWifiConnectedScan according to the wifi-connected flag, for BTC_SCAN_FINISH it calls ActionWifiNotConnected or ActionWifiConnected, and for any other type it does nothing more.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the last branch is 'if START ... else if FINISH' (2289-2299) so other types do nothing, as the prose said; prose tweaked only ('8 slots' replaced by type 8)

name: EXhalbtc8723b1ant_ConnectNotify
prose: Precondition: pBtCoexist is valid with a usable fBtcGet callback; type is any u8 (BTC_ASSOCIATE_START, BTC_ASSOCIATE_FINISH or other). Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns immediately when bManualControl, bStopCoexDm or btInfo.bBtDisabled is set. Otherwise, for BTC_ASSOCIATE_START it sets pCoexSta->bWiFiIsHighPriTask = true and pCoexDm->nArpCnt = 0; for any other type it sets bWiFiIsHighPriTask = false. It then reads the wifi link status; if the link count (status >> 16) is at least 2 it calls LimitedTx(NORMAL_EXEC, 0, 0, 0, 0), LimitedRx(NORMAL_EXEC, false, false, 5) and ActionWifiMultiPort and returns. Otherwise it reads the BT-HS-operation flag; if bC2hBtInquiryPage is set it calls ActionBtInquiry and returns; else if BT HS is on it calls ActionHs and returns; else for BTC_ASSOCIATE_START it calls ActionWifiNotConnectedAssoAuth, for BTC_ASSOCIATE_FINISH it reads the wifi-connected flag and calls ActionWifiNotConnected or ActionWifiConnected, and for any other type it does nothing more.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): old precondition restricted type to START/FINISH although the code handles other values (2320-2323, 2343-2351)

name: ODM_TXPowerTrackingCallback_ThermalMeter
prose: Precondition: Adapter is initialised; ConfigureTxpowerTrack supplies valid callbacks, delta-swing tables, ThermalRegAddr, AverageThermalNum (no larger than the ThermalValue_AVG array) and swing table sizes. Postcondition: returns nothing. It increments RFCalibrateInfo.TXPowerTrackingCallbackCnt, sets bTXPowerTrackingInit = true and reads the thermal value from RF path A. If TxPowerTrackControl is 0 or EEPROMThermalMeter is 0 or 0xFF it returns at that point; the thermal ring, TXPowercount and all other calibration state are untouched. Otherwise it stores the reading at ThermalValue_AVG[ThermalValue_AVG_index], advances the index (wrapping to 0 at AverageThermalNum), averages the nonzero ring entries into ThermalValue (kept as the raw reading if all entries are zero), computes delta against RFCalibrateInfo.ThermalValue and delta_LCK against ThermalValue_LCK; if delta_LCK >= Threshold_IQK it sets ThermalValue_LCK = ThermalValue and calls PHY_LCCalibrate if non-NULL. If delta > 0 (tracking enabled), delta becomes |ThermalValue - EEPROMThermalMeter| capped at TXPWR_TRACK_TABLE_SIZE-1; DeltaPowerIndexLast/DeltaPowerIndex and Absolute_OFDMSwingIdx are updated from the TUP tables when ThermalValue > EEPROMThermalMeter and from the negated TDOWN tables otherwise, for path A and, when RfPathCount > 1, path B. For each configured path PowerIndexOffset is 0 if DeltaPowerIndex equals DeltaPowerIndexLast and their difference otherwise; OFDM_index = BbSwingIdxOfdmBase + offset, and CCK_index = BbSwingIdxCckBase + offset (recomputed in each path iteration); BbSwingIdxCck and BbSwingIdxOfdm[p] are set from these values BEFORE clamping, and then OFDM_index is clamped (above to SwingTableSize_OFDM-1, below to OFDM_min_index, which is 0) and CCK_index (above to SwingTableSize_CCK-1). If delta is 0, PowerIndexOffset of every configured path is set to 0 and the swing indices are not changed. If PowerIndexOffset[A] or [B] is nonzero (and tracking is enabled) it sets bTxPowerChanged, calls ODM_TxPwrTrackSetPwr(MIX_MODE, p, x) for each configured path with x = 0 (Indexforchannel is a local that stays 0, so both branches pass 0), copies the unclamped BbSwingIdxCck and BbSwingIdxOfdm[p] into the Base fields and stores ThermalValue in RFCalibrateInfo.ThermalValue. Finally it sets TXPowercount = 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): BbSwingIdxOfdm/Cck are copied at lines 216-220, before the clamps at 223-229; Base values therefore record the unclamped numbers

name: PHY_SetTxPowerLimit
prose: Slice cut the head: the code is the tail of PHY_SetTxPowerLimit(Adapter, Regulation, Bandwidth, RateSection, RfPath, Channel, PowerLimit) (hal_com_phycfg.c:801-852), not an unnamed function. Precondition: Adapter's HAL data is initialised; all six string arguments point to readable NUL-terminated byte strings (eqNByte compares the first 3, 4 or 2 bytes of each); Channel and PowerLimit hold decimal digits. Postcondition: returns nothing and takes no locks. Channel and PowerLimit are parsed as unsigned 8-bit decimal numbers (a non-digit stops the parse and the partial value is used; the failure result is ignored); powerLimit is held in a signed 8-bit variable and is capped at MAX_POWER_INDEX (0x3F). The regulation index is 0 (FCC), 1 (MKK), 2 (ETSI) or 3 (WW13) by prefix match and stays 0 if none matches; the bandwidth index is 0 for "20M", 1 for "40M" and stays 0 if neither matches. The rate section is 0, 1 or 2 only for RateSection "CCK", "OFDM" or "HT" together with RfPath "1T"; otherwise the function returns without changing anything. The channel index is Channel - 1 (as s8); if it is -1 (Channel parsed as 0) the function returns unchanged. There is no upper range check on the channel index. Otherwise TxPwrLimit_2_4G[regulation][bandwidth][rateSection][channelIndex][RF_PATH_A] is replaced by powerLimit only if powerLimit is smaller than its current value.
note: slice cut head; real function PHY_SetTxPowerLimit; old prose was wrong that an unmatched regulation or bandwidth leaves the table unchanged: both default to index 0 (lines 812, 820-841); channel validity is not range-checked, only -1 is rejected

name: ODM_CfoTracking
prose: Precondition: pDM_VOID points to an initialised struct dm_odm_t (DM_CfoTrack, SupportAbility, bLinked, bOneEntryOnly, bBtEnabled valid). Postcondition: returns nothing. It reads the stored CrystalCap into a local. It returns without change if SupportAbility lacks ODM_BB_CFO_TRACKING. If bLinked is false or bOneEntryOnly is false it calls ODM_CfoTrackingReset (DefXCap = default crystal cap, bAdjust = true, crystal cap set to DefXCap and ATC status set to true, each hardware write only when the stored value changes) and returns. Otherwise: if packetCount equals packetCount_pre it returns; else packetCount_pre = packetCount and CFO_ave = (CFO_tail[0] * 3125) / 1280. If |CFO_ave_pre - CFO_ave| > 20, largeCFOHit is 0 and bAdjust is false, it sets largeCFOHit = 1 and returns (CFO_ave_pre not updated); else it clears largeCFOHit and sets CFO_ave_pre = CFO_ave. bAdjust false becomes true when CFO_ave > CFO_TH_XTAL_HIGH (20) or < -20; bAdjust true becomes false when CFO_ave is strictly between -CFO_TH_XTAL_LOW (10) and +10. If bBtEnabled, bAdjust is forced false and the crystal cap is set to DefXCap (odm_SetCrystalCap, which writes the register only if the stored cap differs). If bAdjust is true: Adjust_Xtal = 1 + ((CFO_ave - 10) >> 2) when CFO_ave > 10, or 1 + ((10 - CFO_ave) >> 2) when CFO_ave < -10 (note: this uses 10 - CFO_ave, not the excess below -10), otherwise 1; the local cap is increased by Adjust_Xtal when CFO_ave > 10, decreased when CFO_ave < -10, unchanged otherwise, clamped to 0..0x3f and passed to odm_SetCrystalCap (a no-op if it equals the stored cap). Finally, in this non-reset path, the ATC status is set to false when |CFO_ave| < CFO_TH_ATC (80) and to true otherwise, writing the BB register only if the stored status changes.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): negative branch uses CFO_TH_XTAL_LOW - CFO_ave (lines 159-160); R1 and R2 claims were already covered by the prose (unsupported ability returns first; equal-to-threshold leaves cap unchanged)

name: SetHwReg8723B
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is SetHwReg8723B(padapter, variable, val) (rtl8723b_hal_init.c:2328-2763). Precondition: padapter is valid and val points to a readable buffer of the width the selected variable needs: u32 for HW_VAR_AC_PARAM_VO/VI/BE/BK, HW_VAR_INITIAL_GAIN, HW_VAR_NAV_UPPER, HW_VAR_MACID_SLEEP and HW_VAR_MACID_WAKEUP; two u32 for HW_VAR_CAM_WRITE; u16 for HW_VAR_BEACON_INTERVAL, HW_VAR_EFUSE_BYTES, HW_VAR_EFUSE_BT_BYTES and HW_VAR_H2C_MEDIA_STATUS_RPT; four bytes for HW_VAR_RESP_SIFS; one byte for the other variables that read *val. val is not dereferenced for HW_VAR_H2C_PS_TUNE_PARAM, HW_VAR_FIFO_CLEARN_UP, HW_VAR_BCN_VALID, HW_VAR_DL_BCN_SEL, HW_VAR_DO_IQK, HW_VAR_DL_RSVD_PAGE, HW_VAR_CAM_INVALID_ALL, HW_VAR_ON_RCR_AM and HW_VAR_OFF_RCR_AM (it is passed along for the delegated ones). Postcondition: returns nothing; one switch case runs per variable. HW_VAR_MEDIA_STATUS writes MSR = (MSR & 0x0c) | *val; HW_VAR_MEDIA_STATUS1 writes MSR = (MSR & 0x03) | (*val << 2). HW_VAR_SET_OPMODE, MAC_ADDR, BSSID, BCN_FUNC, CORRECT_TSF and MLME_DISCONNECT call their hw_var_set_* helpers. HW_VAR_BASIC_RATE builds BrateCfg with HalSetBrateCfg, ORs in 1M/5.5M/11M, ANDs with the allow mask (24M, 12M, 6M, CCK rates), adds 6M for a Cisco peer whose result has none of 24M/12M/6M, stores it in pHalData->BasicRateSet, writes REG_RRSR (16 bit) and clears the low nibble of REG_RRSR+2. TXPAUSE writes *val to REG_TXPAUSE. CHECK_BSSID sets or clears RCR_CBSSID_DATA|RCR_CBSSID_BCN in REG_RCR. MLME_SITESURVEY calls hw_var_set_mlme_sitesurvey then hal_btcoex_ScanNotify(*val != 0). MLME_JOIN calls hw_var_set_mlme_join then hal_btcoex_ConnectNotify(true) for *val == 0, (false) for 1 and nothing for other values. ON/OFF_RCR_AM set/clear RCR_AM. BEACON_INTERVAL, SLOT_TIME, RESP_SIFS (val[0..3] to the CCK and OFDM SIFS register pairs), ACK_PREAMBLE (0x80 if *val else 0 to REG_RRSR+2) write their registers. CAM_EMPTY_ENTRY writes CAM_CONTENT_COUNT words for that entry (first with index bits and the AES algorithm id, the rest 0); CAM_INVALID_ALL writes BIT(31)|BIT(30) to RWCAM; CAM_WRITE writes cam_val[0] to WCAMI and CAM_POLLINIG|CAM_WRITE|cam_val[1] to RWCAM. AC_PARAM_VO/VI/BE/BK write the EDCA registers (BE also stored in pHalData->AcParam_BE). ACM_CTRL writes REG_ACMHWCTRL with AcmHw_HwEn plus BE/VI/VO enable for bits 1/2/3 of *val, or 0 when *val is 0. AMPDU_FACTOR writes (0x2000 << *val) - 1 when *val < HT_AGG_SIZE_32K, else 0x7fff, to REG_AMPDU_MAX_LENGTH_8723B. H2C_FW_PWRMODE calls ODM_RF_Saving(..., true) if the mode is not PS_MODE_ACTIVE, then rtl8723b_set_FwPwrMode_cmd; H2C_PS_TUNE_PARAM, H2C_FW_JOINBSSRPT and H2C_MEDIA_STATUS_RPT (low byte status, high byte macid) send firmware commands. INITIAL_GAIN: 0xff restores DM_DigTable.BackupIGValue through ODM_Write_DIG, any other value saves CurIGValue into BackupIGValue and writes the new gain. EFUSE_USAGE and EFUSE_BYTES store into pHalData; EFUSE_BT_USAGE and EFUSE_BT_BYTES store into pHalData->EfuseHal (HAL_EFUSE_MEMORY is defined in rtl8723b_hal.h). FIFO_CLEARN_UP writes 0xff to REG_TXPAUSE, saves REG_NQOS_SEQ into xmitpriv.nqos_ssn and, unless pwrpriv->bkeepfwalive is set, sets RW_RELEASE_EN in REG_RXPKT_NUM, polls RXDMA_IDLE up to 100 times, writes 0 to REG_RQPN_NPQ and 0x80000000 to REG_RQPN and delays 2 ms. APFM_ON_MAC stores *val in bMacPwrCtrlOn. NAV_UPPER does nothing when the u32 exceeds HAL_NAV_UPPER_UNIT_8723B*0xFF, else writes DIV_ROUND_UP(value, unit) to REG_NAV_UPPER. BCN_VALID sets bit 0 of REG_TDECTRL+2; DL_BCN_SEL clears bit 4 of REG_DWBCN1_CTRL_8723B+2; DO_IQK sets bNeedIQK; DL_RSVD_PAGE downloads the AP-mode BTCoex page in WIFI_AP_STATE and otherwise the normal page. MACID_SLEEP/WAKEUP do nothing for ids above 31 or if the REG_MACID_SLEEP bit is already in the requested state, else set/clear that bit. Any other selector is passed to SetHwReg. No locks are taken and val remains owned by the caller.
note: slice cut head; reviewer RIGHT (R15): REG_RQPN gets 0x80000000, not 0 (line 2667); old prose also merged MEDIA_STATUS and MEDIA_STATUS1 and was contradictory for EFUSE_BT cases

name: sm750_hw_copyarea
prose: Precondition: accel is a valid lynx_accel with usable de_wait and dpr registers; Bpp is nonzero (dPitch and sPitch are divided by it); no locks or references are taken. Postcondition: the direction starts as LEFT_TO_RIGHT. Only when sBase == dBase and sPitch == dPitch is it changed: BOTTOM_TO_TOP if sy < dy, TOP_TO_BOTTOM if sy > dy, and for sy == dy RIGHT_TO_LEFT if sx <= dx, else LEFT_TO_RIGHT. When the direction is BOTTOM_TO_TOP or RIGHT_TO_LEFT, sx and dx are increased by width - 1 and sy and dy by height - 1. It then writes DE_WINDOW_SOURCE_BASE, DE_WINDOW_DESTINATION_BASE, DE_PITCH and DE_WINDOW_WIDTH, and calls accel->de_wait(); if that returns nonzero the function returns -1 and the DE_SOURCE, DE_DESTINATION, DE_DIMENSION and DE_CONTROL registers are not written (the four earlier registers were). Otherwise it writes DE_SOURCE, DE_DESTINATION and DE_DIMENSION, writes DE_CONTROL with rop2, DE_CONTROL_ROP_SELECT, DE_CONTROL_COMMAND_BITBLT and DE_CONTROL_STATUS (plus DE_CONTROL_DIRECTION only for RIGHT_TO_LEFT) and returns 0.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): de_wait is called after the base/pitch/width registers (266) and only the source/dest/dimension/control writes are skipped, exactly what the prose said; R1 claim (direction only for same surface) was also already stated

name: vchiq_close_service_internal
prose: Slice cut the head: vchiq_close_service_internal(service, close_recvd) (vchiq_core.c:3156-3271). Precondition: service is valid; close_recvd is nonzero when the close came from the peer. For service states OPEN and OPENSYNC the code does not expect the caller to hold state->slot_mutex, because queue_message takes it itself. Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno (-EINVAL, -EAGAIN or an error from queue_message or close_service_complete). By service state: CLOSED, HIDDEN, LISTENING or CLOSEWAIT: if close_recvd, logs an error and returns 0; else a non-server service is freed with vchiq_free_service_internal; a server in LISTENING gets status -EINVAL, a server in the other three states gets client_id = 0 and remoteport = VCHIQ_PORT_FREE (and CLOSEWAIT moves to LISTENING); in both server cases remove_event is completed. OPENING: with close_recvd the state becomes CLOSEWAIT and remove_event is completed; otherwise queue_message sends the close message and its result is returned. OPENSYNC: locks state->sync_mutex first, then as OPEN. OPEN/OPENSYNC: with close_recvd, do_abort_bulks failing gives -EAGAIN; release_service_messages is called; if no error so far it queues the close message with QMFLAGS_NO_MUTEX_UNLOCK (queue_message takes slot_mutex and keeps it on success, and releases it itself on its own failures). On any error sync_mutex is unlocked if the state is OPENSYNC and the function returns the error with slot_mutex not held. On success slot_mutex (and sync_mutex when service->sync) is unlocked and the state is CLOSESENT (close not received) or CLOSERECVD (close received, then the result of close_service_complete is returned). CLOSESENT: nothing if close was not received, else -EAGAIN if do_abort_bulks fails, else the result of close_service_complete. CLOSERECVD: a server with close not received is forced to LISTENING; then the result of close_service_complete. Any other state logs an error and returns 0.
note: reviewer R15 RIGHT (LISTENING server -EINVAL path still completes remove_event, line 3191); R2 claim WRONG: queue_message (lines 960-962, 1053-1054, 1161) takes slot_mutex itself and releases it on failure, so error paths do not leave it held; old precondition 'caller holds slot_mutex' was unsupported

name: fake_master_set
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is fake_master_set(image, enabled, vme_base, size, aspace, cycle, dwidth) (vme_fake.c:251-332); the name __fake_master_set does not exist. Precondition: image is a valid master window resource whose parent bridge has driver_priv set. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL, with a message, and does not take image->lock or modify the stored window if any of these hold: vme_base has any of its low 16 bits set, size has any of its low 16 bits set, size is 0 while enabled is nonzero, dwidth is not VME_D8, VME_D16 or VME_D32, or aspace is not one of VME_A16, VME_A24, VME_A32, VME_A64, VME_CRCSR, VME_USER1..4. Otherwise it takes image->lock (spin_lock), stores enabled, vme_base, size, aspace, cycle and dwidth into bridge->masters[image->number], releases the lock and returns 0. cycle is not validated.
note: slice cut head; real name fake_master_set; prose otherwise verified against lines 255-332

name: cxgbit_target_rx_opcode
prose: Precondition: csk->conn is a valid iSCSI connection and csk->skb carries a received PDU whose header is reachable through cxgbit_rx_pdu_cb. Postcondition: it dispatches on the opcode of the header (hdr->opcode & ISCSI_OPCODE_MASK) and returns the value of the chosen handler: SCSI_CMD (cxgbit_handle_scsi_cmd), SCSI_DATA_OUT (cxgbit_handle_iscsi_dataout, no command allocated), NOOP_OUT (cxgbit_handle_nop_out; a command is allocated only when ttt is 0xFFFFFFFF, otherwise the handler gets NULL), SCSI_TMFUNC (iscsit_handle_task_mgt_cmd), TEXT (cxgbit_handle_text_cmd, with a command found by iscsit_find_cmd_from_itt when ttt is not 0xFFFFFFFF, else newly allocated), LOGOUT (iscsit_handle_logout_cmd; if its result is positive it waits up to SECONDS_FOR_LOGOUT_COMP*HZ on conn->conn_logout_comp, and the handler result is returned) and SNACK (iscsit_handle_snack). If cxgbit_allocate_cmd returns NULL, or the TEXT lookup by itt returns NULL, it returns iscsit_add_reject(conn, ISCSI_REASON_BOOKMARK_NO_RESOURCES, hdr). For any other opcode it logs the opcode, calls dump_stack() and returns -EINVAL (the initial value of ret; the default case does not jump to the reject label). This function does not free a command it allocated: what happens to the command on a handler failure is up to the handler (cxgbit_handle_text_cmd, for example, returns -ENOMEM on a failed text_in allocation without freeing cmd).
note: reviewer R15 RIGHT: cxgbit_handle_text_cmd returns -ENOMEM without freeing cmd (cxgbit_target.c:1186-1192), so old 'freed by that handler' was unsupported; R1 and R2 WRONG: default case breaks with ret still -EINVAL (1272-1278)

name: chap_server_compute_hash
prose: Slice cut the head: the real function is chap_server_compute_hash(conn, auth, nr_in_ptr, nr_out_ptr, nr_out_len) (iscsi_target_auth.c:240-588); the name chap_server_compute_md5 does not exist. Precondition: nr_in_ptr is the NUL-terminated received text parameter string; conn->auth_protocol is an initialised struct iscsi_chap (digest_size, digest_name, id, challenge, challenge_len); auth holds userid, password, password_mutual, userid_mutual and authenticate_target; nr_out_ptr has room for the mutual-authentication reply and nr_out_len is writable. The identifier and response buffers are local to the function. Postcondition: returns 0 on success and -1 on any failure (no other errno is returned); all temporary buffers, the shash descriptor and the tfm are released before returning on each return. It fails for any allocation or crypto error, for a missing CHAP_N, a CHAP_N of HEX type or one that differs from auth->userid (compared including the NUL), a missing or malformed CHAP_R (HEX: exactly 2*digest_size valid hex digits; BASE64: not longer than ceil(4*digest_size/3) after stripping '=' and decoding to exactly digest_size bytes), and when the digest over chap->id, auth->password and chap->challenge differs from the received CHAP_R. If that matches and auth->authenticate_target is false it returns 0 without touching nr_out_ptr. If it is true: a missing CHAP_I (-ENOENT) also returns 0 (initiator uses one-way authentication) with nr_out_ptr untouched; otherwise CHAP_I must parse (HEX or DECIMAL) to at most 255, CHAP_C must be present, HEX or BASE64, decode to 1..1024 bytes and must not equal the target's own challenge (same length and bytes), else the function fails. It then computes the digest over the initiator's identifier, auth->password_mutual and the decoded challenge (this value is only sent, not compared), writes "CHAP_N=<userid_mutual>" NUL "CHAP_R=0x<hex digest>" NUL into nr_out_ptr, sets *nr_out_len to the total length including both NULs and returns 0.
note: slice cut head; real name chap_server_compute_hash; old prose wrongly required CHAP_I/CHAP_C to be present and valid for success (missing CHAP_I returns 0, line 429-433), described a 'response' output buffer supplied by the caller, and said the mutual digest is compared

name: lio_target_call_delnpfromtpg
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is lio_target_call_delnpfromtpg(se_tpg_np) (iscsi_target_configfs.c:247-273); the name lio_target_np_drop_item_callback does not exist. Precondition: se_tpg_np is embedded in a struct iscsi_tpg_np (container_of) whose tpg is valid. Postcondition: returns nothing. If iscsit_get_tpg(tpg) returns a negative value the function returns at once with no further effect. Otherwise it logs the deregistration, calls iscsit_tpg_del_network_portal(tpg, tpg_np), logs "delnpfromtpg done" only when that call returned 0 (a failure is not reported to the caller), and in both cases calls iscsit_put_tpg(tpg) before returning.

name: DEF_DEV_WWN_ASSOC_SHOW(_name, _assoc)
prose: Macro-generated functions target_wwn_vpd_assoc_logical_unit_show (association 0x00), target_wwn_vpd_assoc_target_port_show (0x10) and target_wwn_vpd_assoc_scsi_target_device_show (0x20), all produced by DEF_DEV_WWN_ASSOC_SHOW(_name, _assoc) (the head quoted is the definition at line 1729). Precondition: item is a config_item embedded in a struct t10_wwn (to_t10_wwn) whose t10_vpd_list is a valid list protected by t10_vpd_lock; page points to a writable PAGE_SIZE buffer. Postcondition: it takes t10_wwn->t10_vpd_lock (spin_lock) and walks the list; entries whose association differs from the macro's _assoc are skipped; for each remaining entry it builds, in a local VPD_TMP_BUF_SIZE buffer, the strings from transport_dump_vpd_assoc, transport_dump_vpd_ident_type and transport_dump_vpd_ident one after another and appends each to page with sprintf, but stops the whole loop (breaking before appending that string) as soon as the current length plus the next string's length would be at least PAGE_SIZE. It releases the lock and returns the number of bytes written, which is less than PAGE_SIZE.

name: target_pr_res_aptpl_metadata_store
prose: Real function target_pr_res_aptpl_metadata_store(item, page, count) (target_core_configfs.c:2054-2237), not macro-generated (the slice cut the head). Precondition: item embeds a struct se_device (pr_to_dev) and page is a NUL-terminated string of comma- or newline-separated key=value tokens. Postcondition: returns count immediately, changing nothing, if dev_attrib.emulate_pr is off, if TRANSPORT_FLAG_PASSTHROUGH_PGR is set in transport_flags, or if DRF_SPC2_RESERVATIONS is set in dev_reservation_flags; returns -EINVAL if export_count is nonzero; returns -ENOMEM if kstrdup(page) fails. The copy is then split on ",\n"; unknown tokens are ignored. String options (initiator_fabric, initiator_node, initiator_isid, target_fabric, target_node) are stored with match_strdup (failure: -ENOMEM and exit); a repeated string option overwrites the earlier pointer without freeing it. Numeric options (sa_res_key and mapped_lun/target_lun via match_u64; res_holder, res_type, res_scope, res_all_tg_pt, tpgt, port_rtpi via match_int) return the negative parse error immediately if they fail to parse; res_scope and port_rtpi are parsed but unused. An over-length initiator_node, initiator_isid or target_node only logs and sets ret to -EINVAL and breaks out of the switch; parsing goes on and ret is overwritten by later steps, so the length check alone does not make the function fail. After parsing it returns -EINVAL if initiator_node or target_node was not given or sa_res_key is 0, or if res_holder is nonzero and res_type is 0. Otherwise it returns the result of core_scsi3_alloc_aptpl_registration, mapped to count when that result is 0 and passed on otherwise. After kstrdup succeeds the kstrdup copy and the last-stored string options are freed on each return. page and item are not modified.
note: old prose said 'Generated function' (wrong: ordinary function), omitted that sa_res_key==0 is rejected and that a repeated string option leaks the earlier match_strdup copy
